notes.text: Discovery call with Dana Reyes, practice manager at Harbourline Physio. Dana said the front desk returns voicemails two or three days late and that web form requests are re-typed into the booking system by hand. She estimated they lose about ten new patients a month because nobody calls back in time. We agreed to start with a starter scan of the callback workflow rather than a full assessment. Dana will send last month's missed-call log by Friday. Casey will send the scan agreement on Monday. Next step: kickoff call for the scan on 20 November.

Follow-up call with Marco Bellini of Bellini Plumbing & Drain. Marco confirmed that quote requests arrive by email and sit unanswered for up to a week when he is on jobs. He said his sister Carla does the invoicing at night and is tired of chasing unpaid invoices by phone. Decision: Marco approved the inbound-reply build for quote requests, starting 1 December. Carla will export the last 90 days of quote emails by Wednesday. Casey will draft the reply templates and send them to Marco for review. We will meet again on 28 November to review the templates.

Casey: Thanks for making time, Sofia. What's hurting most at the clinic right now?
Sofia: Honestly, no-shows. We lose four or five appointments a week because reminder calls are made by hand and often get skipped.
Casey: Who makes those calls today?
Sofia: Our receptionist, when she has a free minute. She also copies new patient forms from paper into the system.
Casey: Would it help to see a short scan of the reminder process first?
Sofia: Yes, let's do that. I'll get you read-only access to the booking system by Thursday.
Casey: Great. I'll send the scan outline tomorrow, and we can book the review once you've read it.

Site visit debrief with Owen Clarke, Clarke Roofing. Owen's crew leads text him photos of each job and he builds quotes from them at night; quotes go out three to five days after the visit. He said two commercial jobs were lost last quarter because a competitor quoted first. Agreed: we will pilot a quote-intake form for crew leads on two crews. Owen will pick the two crews by Monday.
Thanks for today. Confirming on my side: I'll send you our current quote template and three recent quotes by Tuesday. One thing we did not settle is who pays for the tablet mounts in the trucks.

notes.text: Scoping call with Helen Marsh, Marsh & Tolland Family Law. Helen said new consultation requests come through a 28-field intake form and a paralegal replies within three business days. She believes people give up on the form halfway. Helen wants a shorter first step but said the partners have not agreed to change the form yet. Helen will raise the intake form at the partners' meeting on 19 November. Casey will send two examples of short intake flows before then. We will speak again after the partners' meeting.

Check-in with Andre Silva, owner of Northgate Fitness. Andre said membership cancellations are handled by a paper form at the front desk and about a third of them are never entered, so people keep getting billed and then dispute the charge. Chargebacks cost him roughly six hours a month to sort out. He agreed to a starter scan of the cancellation process. Andre will send a photo of the cancellation form and last month's chargeback list by Thursday. Casey will book the one-hour walkthrough for next week.

Quarterly check-in with Maya Chen at Chen & Co Bookkeeping. Maya said the reminder system we built is running without problems and she had no new requests. We talked about her office move in the spring. No decisions were made, nobody took on any tasks, and no next meeting was booked.

Planning call with the Tidewater Catering team (Rosa Diaz and two event leads). Rosa said event enquiries arrive through Instagram messages, email and phone, and nobody owns the Instagram inbox on weekends. Someone needs to export last season's enquiry list before the next call. Rosa will ask the event leads how long a quote takes them. It was agreed that the next call will look only at weekend enquiries.

Call with Jonas Weber, Weber Auto Repair. Jonas said customers call to ask if their car is ready eight or ten times a day and it pulls mechanics off the floor. Jonas will send the list of status questions customers ask most by the end of next week. Casey will share a sample status-text flow in two weeks. No start date was set.

Options call with Farah Aziz, Aziz Property Management. Casey presented two options: a tenant-request triage inbox, or a voice agent for after-hours maintenance calls. Farah liked the triage inbox but said she must check the budget with her business partner first. Nothing was chosen today. Farah asked whether the triage inbox can work with their current property software; Casey did not know and will find out. Farah will come back with an answer on budget after she talks to her partner.

Call with Nadia Petrov, Petrov Physio Supplies. Nadia said: “we lose about ten wholesale leads a week” because web enquiries get a reply in > 2 days. Her target is a reply in < 4 hours. She uses a shared inbox <sales@petrov.example> that three people check ‘when they remember’. Nadia will forward one week of enquiries to Casey by Tuesday – unedited.
Quick call with Marco. He'll send photos of the van signage tomorrow.
